AVCC is the ADC reference, so rail sag is current-dependent gain error, which lands on R_s and does not cancel within a sweep. Apparent extra R_s = R_usb x V_F / VCC. 2 mV sag = 0.06 ohm, 10 mV = 0.28 ohm, 20 mV = 0.57 ohm, 40 mV = 1.13 ohm. It IS common to all samples provided the same cable, port and computer are used every session, so log this reading each session and treat a change in it as a session-level offset.

Round 2 step 3, 100 ohm dummy in place of a die, 63 levels captured. Raw file FINAL_MEASUREMENTS/data/R2_sweeps/verify_100R_step3_FAILED.csv. Fit gave slope 99.32 ohm but with a +13.79 mV intercept and 2.16 mV rms residual. A pure resistor must fit through the origin, so the rig FAILED verification. Two independent faults found, neither of them the resistor.

FAULT 1. All three ADC channels read low by a common 10 +/- 2 mV (about 2 counts). Proven two ways: (a) the current deficit versus theory is a constant 11-14 mV across a 30x current range, which is additive not multiplicative; (b) only an offset near 10 mV makes the AVR pin HIGH voltage come out below 5.034 V and falling with current, as it physically must. Independent of ADC prescaler (/32, /64, /128) and of discarding a conversion after each mux change, so it is neither clock speed nor mux settling. It CANCELS in v_die, which is a difference of two channels, but NOT in the current, which is an absolute voltage. Error on i is 26 pct at the bottom of the sweep and 1 pct at the top. Diagnostic matrix in FINAL_MEASUREMENTS/data/R2_sweeps/adc_diag_prescaler_discard.csv.

FAULT 2. A0 and A2 are the same breadboard node by design and must read identically. A0 reads high by an amount strictly proportional to current: 2.9 +/- 0.2 ohm between the two taps, stable over levels 2 to 32. That is contact resistance in the E4-E8 link jumper or its breadboard sockets. It happens to sit outside both the v_die loop and the current tap so it does not corrupt R_s in this topology, but 2.9 ohm is 30x the bond resistances being measured and it is a flaky joint. Reseat it.

FIX for fault 1: measure the sense resistor differentially. Add one jumper from UNO A3 to the GND rail and compute i = (v_A2 - v_A3)/R_SENSE. The ADC offset is common to both channels so it subtracts out exactly, which is precisely why v_die was already unaffected. It also removes the IR drop in the single GND jumper from the current measurement. Requires one extra male-male jumper, a sketch change, and a redraw.

Round 2 step 5. Board 1 D6 red draws no current: i_max 0.146 mA (which is only the 14.4 mV ADC offset over R_SENSE, i.e. zero) and v_die pinned at 5.00 V, the open-circuit signature. This CONFIRMS round 1, where R1_channels.csv already recorded board 1 D6 R as OL, verdict open, while D6 G and B passed at 2.248 and 2.523 V. Two independent instruments, DMM and I-V rig, agree. File kept as s1_D6_R_seat1_OPEN.csv. Not a wiring fault and not a bad capture. R_s is undefined for this channel; exclude it from the fits and count it as an open-junction defect.
